records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: spoke ... saying: the opening of a new speech
decisions.reason: The usual opening of a speech of God to Moses, as in 1:1. The speech runs to the end of the chapter.

records.heading: Do not live like Egypt or Canaan

records.source: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel, and you will say to them, I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.2: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.2: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: I am the LORD your God: God names himself as Israel's own God before he gives his laws
decisions.reason: These words open the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:2), where they are followed by "who brought you out of the land of Egypt". Here too they stand before the commands and give the reason for them: Israel is to live this way because of who its God is and because he has bound himself to this people. The words frame the chapter, returning in verses 4 and 30, and the shorter "I am the LORD" marks off the laws in verses 5, 6 and 21. The same refrain runs through chapters 19-26 (19:2-4; 20:7; 22:33; 26:13).

decisions.choice: speak to the Israelites and say to them: the laws are for the whole people
decisions.reason: As in 1:2. Moses is to pass the words on to all Israel, not only to the priests.

decisions.choice: I [am]
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "I the LORD your God" with no verb. Literal brackets the "am" that English needs; Balanced and Readable write it plainly.

records.source: כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֧ה אֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֛יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְשַׁבְתֶּם־בָּ֖הּ לֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֑וּ וּכְמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה אֶֽרֶץ־כְּנַ֡עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא אֶתְכֶ֥ם שָׁ֨מָּה֙ לֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֔וּ וּבְחֻקֹּתֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֥א תֵלֵֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: According to [the] deed[s] of [the] land of Egypt, in which you dwelt, not you will do; and according to [the] deed[s] of [the] land of Canaan, where I [am] bringing you there, not you will do; and in their statutes not you will walk.
pieces: Do not copy what is done in the land of Egypt, where you once lived, or what is done in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not live by their customs.

L.3: According to the deeds of the land of Egypt, in which you dwelt, you shall not do; and according to the deeds of the land of Canaan, to which I am bringing you, you shall not do; and in their statutes you shall not walk.

R.3: You once lived in Egypt. Do not do the things people do there. I am bringing you into the land of Canaan. Do not do the things people do there either. Do not follow their ways of life.

decisions.choice: the deeds of the land of Egypt and of the land of Canaan: the practices of the peoples Israel has left and is about to meet
decisions.reason: Israel stands between the land it left and the land it is going to. "The deeds" are the practices the chapter goes on to list (verses 6-23), and verses 24-30 say that the peoples of Canaan did them. Marriage between brother and sister is attested in Egypt's royal family, and the Bible records child sacrifice among the peoples around Israel (Deuteronomy 12:31; 18:9-10; 2 Kings 3:27). The chapter does not claim that every item on the list was the custom of both lands.

decisions.choice: walk in their statutes: live by their established customs
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for God's own statutes in verse 4. Here it means the fixed customs of the nations, and the two ways of life are set against each other: not their statutes but mine. To "walk" in something is to live by it (26:3; Deuteronomy 8:6). The word returns in verse 30 for "the customs" of the nations.

decisions.choice: customs (Balanced); ways of life (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "statutes", the word used for God's laws in verse 4. Balanced and Readable say "customs" and "ways of life", because the statutes of the nations are not laws God gave but the customs they keep.

decisions.choice: You once lived in Egypt ... I am bringing you into the land of Canaan
decisions.reason: Readable states each place first and then gives the command, in short sentences.

records.source: אֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֧י תַּעֲשׂ֛וּ וְאֶת־חֻקֹּתַ֥י תִּשְׁמְר֖וּ לָלֶ֣כֶת בָּהֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: My judgments you will do, and my statutes you will keep, to walk in them; I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: You are to carry out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, living by them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.4: My judgments you shall do, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes you shall keep, walking in them; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.4: Do what {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules say, and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws. Let them guide the way you live. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: judgments and statutes: God's rulings and his fixed decrees, together the whole of his law
decisions.reason: The first word is a ruling or judgment, the kind of decision a judge gives in a case; it often names laws stated as cases ("if a man ...", Exodus 21:1). The second is a statute, a decree fixed by authority. Leviticus often pairs the two (verses 5 and 26; 19:37; 20:22; 25:18; 26:15), and together they mean all that God commands. They stand against "their statutes" in verse 3: Israel is to live by God's law, not by the customs of the nations.

decisions.choice: to walk in them: to make them the way one lives
decisions.reason: As in verse 3. The laws are not only to be kept on occasion but to shape the whole of life.

decisions.choice: rulings, statutes (Balanced); rules, laws (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "judgments" and "statutes". Balanced says "rulings" and "statutes", and Readable "rules" and "laws", the wording used for these words throughout Leviticus.

decisions.choice: Let them guide the way you live
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "walk in them" instead of reproducing it.

records.source: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־חֻקֹּתַי֙ וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֛ם הָאָדָ֖ם וָחַ֣י בָּהֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And you will keep my statutes and my judgments, which will do them the human and he will live by them; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings. The one who does them will live by them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.5: And you shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments, which a person shall do and he shall live by them; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.5: Keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and rules. Anyone who obeys them will have life because of them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a person who does them will live by them: life is promised to the one who keeps God's laws
decisions.reason: To "live" here is to have life under God's blessing: to stay alive, to remain in the land and to prosper there (Deuteronomy 4:1; 30:15-20). The laws are given to a people God has already brought out of Egypt (verse 3), and keeping them is the way that people is to go on living. The words are repeated in Ezekiel 20:11, 13, 21 and Nehemiah 9:29. In the New Testament, Paul quotes them in Romans 10:5 and Galatians 3:12 to describe the righteousness that is based on the law, which he sets against the righteousness that comes by faith.

decisions.choice: the human: any person
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being, not the word for a man or for an Israelite. The promise is stated for anyone who keeps these laws.

decisions.choice: by them: by means of them, or in them
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "by" (life comes through keeping the laws) or "in" (the laws are the sphere in which one lives). Both senses belong together, and the renderings keep "by", as in Romans 10:5 and Galatians 3:12.

decisions.choice: will have life because of them
decisions.reason: Readable says what "live by them" means: life comes to those who obey these laws. Literal and Balanced keep "live by them", the wording that Romans 10:5 and Galatians 3:12 quote.

records.source: אִ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ אֶל־כָּל־שְׁאֵ֣ר בְּשָׂר֔וֹ לֹ֥א תִקְרְב֖וּ לְגַלּ֣וֹת עֶרְוָ֑ה אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: [A] man, [a] man, to any relative of his flesh not you will draw near to uncover nakedness; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Not one of you is to go near any close relative of his own flesh to have sexual relations. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.6: Any man [of you]: to any relative of his own flesh you shall not draw near to uncover nakedness; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.6: A man must never go to someone in his own family to have sexual relations. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: to uncover nakedness: to have sexual intercourse
decisions.reason: "Nakedness" is the uncovered body, the private parts (Genesis 9:22-23; Exodus 20:26). To "uncover the nakedness" of someone is a plain Hebrew way of saying to have sexual relations with them. In this chapter it covers both a casual act and a marriage: verses 17 and 18 forbid "taking" a woman, that is marrying her, to uncover her nakedness. Chapter 20 repeats most of these laws with their penalties (20:11-21).

decisions.choice: relative of his flesh: a close blood relative
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means kin, those of one's own body and blood (Genesis 2:23-24; 29:14). The list that follows (verses 7-17) spells out who counts: parents and step-parents, sisters and half-sisters, granddaughters, aunts, and the wives of close male relatives, who are counted as family through marriage.

decisions.choice: a man, a man ... you will not draw near: each one of you men must not approach
decisions.reason: The doubled word means "any man", "each one" (17:3). The sentence starts with "a man" and goes on with "you" (plural), so the law is spoken to the men of Israel one by one. To "draw near" to a woman is itself a way of speaking of sexual relations (verses 14 and 19; 20:16; Genesis 20:4; Isaiah 8:3).

decisions.choice: have sexual relations
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "uncover nakedness". Balanced and Readable say what it means, here and throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: Any man [of you]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "of you" to link the opening "a man, a man" with the "you" of the command.

records.heading: Forbidden sexual relations

records.source: עֶרְוַ֥ת אָבִ֛יךָ וְעֶרְוַ֥ת אִמְּךָ֖ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה אִמְּךָ֣ הִ֔וא לֹ֥א תְגַלֶּ֖ה עֶרְוָתָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of your father and [the] nakedness of your mother not you will uncover; your mother she [is]; not you will uncover her nakedness.
pieces: You must not have sexual relations with your mother, for that would be an offense against your father. She is your mother. Do not have sexual relations with her.

L.7: The nakedness of your father and the nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover; she [is] your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

R.7: Do not have sexual relations with your mother. That would be a wrong against your father. She is your mother. Do not have sexual relations with her.

decisions.choice: the nakedness of your father and of your mother: your father's nakedness, that is, your mother's
alternatives: your father's nakedness and your mother's nakedness (two separate bans)
decisions.reason: The "and" most likely explains rather than adds: to lie with one's mother is to uncover what belongs to one's father. Verse 8 and 20:11 speak the same way of the father's wife ("it is your father's nakedness"), and the rest of the verse speaks only of the mother. The words could also be read as two separate bans, on relations with one's father and with one's mother (compare Genesis 9:22).

decisions.choice: she is your mother: the reason stated in a short clause
decisions.reason: Each law in verses 7-17 gives its reason in a short clause naming the relationship, so that the bond itself is the reason.

decisions.choice: that would be an offense against your father (Balanced); That would be a wrong against your father (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state what "the nakedness of your father" means here: to lie with one's mother wrongs one's father. Literal keeps the Hebrew wording.

records.source: עֶרְוַ֥ת אֵֽשֶׁת־אָבִ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה עֶרְוַ֥ת אָבִ֖יךָ הִֽוא׃ס
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of [the] wife of your father not you will uncover; [the] nakedness of your father it [is].
pieces: Do not have sexual relations with your father's wife. That would be an offense against your father.

L.8: The nakedness of your father's wife you shall not uncover; it [is] the nakedness of your father.

R.8: Do not have sexual relations with your father's wife. That would be a wrong against your father.

decisions.choice: your father's wife: a wife of your father other than your mother
decisions.reason: Your mother is covered in verse 7. A man could have more than one wife, so this is another wife of one's father, or a stepmother. The ban holds after the father's death as well (20:11; Deuteronomy 22:30; 27:20). Reuben's act with his father's concubine was remembered against him (Genesis 35:22; 49:4), and Paul condemns a man living with his father's wife (1 Corinthians 5:1).

decisions.choice: it is your father's nakedness: it violates your father's own marriage
decisions.reason: The father and his wife are one flesh (Genesis 2:24), so to uncover her is to uncover him. The wrong is done against the father himself.

decisions.choice: That would be an offense against your father (Balanced); a wrong against your father (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7. Literal keeps "it is the nakedness of your father".

records.source: עֶרְוַ֨ת אֲחֽוֹתְךָ֤ בַת־אָבִ֨יךָ֙ א֣וֹ בַת־אִמֶּ֔ךָ מוֹלֶ֣דֶת בַּ֔יִת א֖וֹ מוֹלֶ֣דֶת ח֑וּץ לֹ֥א תְגַלֶּ֖ה עֶרְוָתָֽן׃ס
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of your sister, [the] daughter of your father or [the] daughter of your mother, born [at] home or born outside, not you will uncover their nakedness.
pieces: You must not have sexual relations with a sister of yours, the daughter of your father or of your mother, whether she was born into your household or born outside it.

L.9: The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother, born at home or born outside, you shall not uncover their nakedness.

R.9: Do not have sexual relations with your sister or half sister. It does not matter if she is the daughter of your father or of your mother. It does not matter if she was born in your family's home or somewhere else.

decisions.choice: your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother: a full sister or a half-sister
decisions.reason: A half-sister on either side is as forbidden as a full sister (20:17; Deuteronomy 27:22). Earlier, Abraham had married Sarah, his father's daughter by another mother (Genesis 20:12); this law forbids such a marriage in Israel. Tamar's words to Amnon in 2 Samuel 13:12-13 show it was counted a disgrace.

decisions.choice: born at home or born outside: born into your household or into another
alternatives: born in wedlock or out of wedlock
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means a sister brought up in your own household or one born elsewhere, for example a daughter of your mother by an earlier husband, who grew up in another home. It may instead set a daughter born within a marriage against one born outside it. Either way the point is that every sister is included.

decisions.choice: your sister or half sister
decisions.reason: Readable names the half-sister directly, which is what "the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother" includes.

records.source: עֶרְוַ֤ת בַּת־בִּנְךָ֙ א֣וֹ בַֽת־בִּתְּךָ֔ לֹ֥א תְגַלֶּ֖ה עֶרְוָתָ֑ן כִּ֥י עֶרְוָתְךָ֖ הֵֽנָּה׃ס
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of [the] daughter of your son or [the] daughter of your daughter, not you will uncover their nakedness, for your [own] nakedness they [are].
pieces: You must not have sexual relations with your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, for they are your own flesh and blood.

L.10: The nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, you shall not uncover their nakedness; for they [are] your own nakedness.

R.10: Do not have sexual relations with your granddaughter. She is your own flesh and blood.

decisions.choice: they are your own nakedness: they come from your own body
decisions.reason: A granddaughter is descended from the man himself, so to uncover her is, in the chapter's terms, to uncover himself. The phrase is like "your father's nakedness" in verse 8.

decisions.choice: son's daughter or daughter's daughter: the chapter does not name a man's own daughter
decisions.reason: The list has no separate law for a man's own daughter. Verse 17 forbids a woman and her daughter, and the reason given here, that one's descendants are one's own flesh, applies all the more to a daughter.

decisions.choice: your own flesh and blood
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a familiar phrase for one's own descendants. Literal keeps "your own nakedness".

decisions.choice: your granddaughter
decisions.reason: Readable uses one word for the son's daughter and the daughter's daughter.

records.source: עֶרְוַ֨ת בַּת־אֵ֤שֶׁת אָבִ֨יךָ֙ מוֹלֶ֣דֶת אָבִ֔יךָ אֲחוֹתְךָ֖ הִ֑וא לֹ֥א תְגַלֶּ֖ה עֶרְוָתָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of [the] daughter of [the] wife of your father, born [to] your father, your sister she [is]; not you will uncover her nakedness.
pieces: Your father's wife may have borne him a daughter; she is your sister, and you must not have sexual relations with her.

L.11: The nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born [to] your father, she [is] your sister; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

R.11: Your father may have a daughter by another wife. She is your sister. Do not have sexual relations with her.

decisions.choice: the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father: a half-sister by another wife of your father
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, "your father's wife" is a wife other than your mother. Verse 9 has already forbidden a half-sister; this verse repeats the ban for the case where the girl's mother is another wife in the same family, and states plainly that she is your sister.

decisions.choice: Your father's wife may have borne him a daughter (Balanced); Your father may have a daughter by another wife (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the case first and then the ban. Readable says "another wife", following the meaning of "your father's wife" in verse 8.

records.source: עֶרְוַ֥ת אֲחוֹת־אָבִ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה שְׁאֵ֥ר אָבִ֖יךָ הִֽוא׃ס
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of [the] sister of your father not you will uncover; [the] relative of your father she [is].
pieces: You must not have sexual relations with your father's sister. She is your father's blood relative.

L.12: The nakedness of your father's sister you shall not uncover; she [is] your father's own flesh.

R.12: Do not have sexual relations with your father's sister. She is part of your father's own family.

decisions.choice: your father's sister ... your father's relative: your aunt, a blood relative of your father
decisions.reason: The word for relative is the "flesh" of verse 6. Before the law was given, Amram had married his father's sister Jochebed, the mother of Moses and Aaron (Exodus 6:20). Chapter 20 repeats the ban (20:19).

records.source: עֶרְוַ֥ת אֲחֽוֹת־אִמְּךָ֖ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה כִּֽי־שְׁאֵ֥ר אִמְּךָ֖ הִֽוא׃ס
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of [the] sister of your mother not you will uncover, for [the] relative of your mother she [is].
pieces: You must not have sexual relations with your mother's sister, for she is your mother's blood relative.

L.13: The nakedness of your mother's sister you shall not uncover, for she [is] your mother's own flesh.

R.13: Do not have sexual relations with your mother's sister. She is part of your mother's own family.

decisions.choice: your mother's sister: your aunt on your mother's side
decisions.reason: The same ban as verse 12, for the mother's side of the family (20:19).

records.source: עֶרְוַ֥ת אֲחִֽי־אָבִ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה אֶל־אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ לֹ֣א תִקְרָ֔ב דֹּדָֽתְךָ֖ הִֽוא׃ס
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of [the] brother of your father not you will uncover; to his wife not you will draw near; your aunt she [is].
pieces: Do not go near the wife of your father's brother to have sexual relations with her, for that would be an offense against your uncle. She is your aunt.

L.14: The nakedness of your father's brother you shall not uncover; to his wife you shall not draw near; she [is] your aunt.

R.14: Do not have sexual relations with the wife of your father's brother. That would be a wrong against your uncle. She is your aunt.

decisions.choice: uncover the nakedness of your father's brother ... do not draw near to his wife: to lie with his wife is to wrong him
decisions.reason: The second clause explains the first. The uncle's "nakedness" is uncovered when someone lies with his wife, as in verse 8 for the father. To "draw near" is the idiom of verse 6.

decisions.choice: your aunt: the wife of your father's brother
decisions.reason: The word means an uncle's wife. She is related by marriage, not by blood, and is still counted as family (20:20).

decisions.choice: Do not go near the wife ... for that would be an offense against your uncle
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the act first and then say why it wrongs the uncle. Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

records.source: עֶרְוַ֥ת כַּלָּֽתְךָ֖ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה אֵ֤שֶׁת בִּנְךָ֙ הִ֔וא לֹ֥א תְגַלֶּ֖ה עֶרְוָתָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of your daughter-in-law not you will uncover; [the] wife of your son she [is]; not you will uncover her nakedness.
pieces: You must not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law. She is married to your son. Do not have sexual relations with her.

L.15: The nakedness of your daughter-in-law you shall not uncover; she [is] your son's wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

R.15: Do not have sexual relations with your son's wife. She is your daughter-in-law. Do not have sexual relations with her.

decisions.choice: your daughter-in-law: your son's wife
decisions.reason: Chapter 20 makes this a crime for which both die (20:12). Judah lay with his daughter-in-law Tamar without knowing who she was (Genesis 38:15-18, 26).

records.source: עֶרְוַ֥ת אֵֽשֶׁת־אָחִ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה עֶרְוַ֥ת אָחִ֖יךָ הִֽוא׃ס
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of [the] wife of your brother not you will uncover; [the] nakedness of your brother it [is].
pieces: You must not have sexual relations with the wife of your brother. It would be an offense against him.

L.16: The nakedness of your brother's wife you shall not uncover; it [is] the nakedness of your brother.

R.16: Do not have sexual relations with your brother's wife. That would be a wrong against your brother.

decisions.choice: your brother's wife: forbidden while she is his wife, and after
decisions.reason: Chapter 20 repeats the ban (20:21). Deuteronomy 25:5-10 makes one exception: when a man dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow so that the dead man's name goes on. John the Baptist condemned Herod Antipas for marrying his brother's wife (Mark 6:17-18).

decisions.choice: it is your brother's nakedness: it wrongs your brother himself
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: It would be an offense against him (Balanced); a wrong against your brother (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8. Literal keeps "it is the nakedness of your brother".

records.source: עֶרְוַ֥ת אִשָּׁ֛ה וּבִתָּ֖הּ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה אֶֽת־בַּת־בְּנָ֞הּ וְאֶת־בַּת־בִּתָּ֗הּ לֹ֤א תִקַּח֙ לְגַלּ֣וֹת עֶרְוָתָ֔הּ שַׁאֲרָ֥ה הֵ֖נָּה זִמָּ֥ה הִֽוא
records.gloss: [The] nakedness of [a] woman and her daughter not you will uncover; the daughter of her son and the daughter of her daughter not you will take to uncover her nakedness; relatives they [are]; depravity it [is].
pieces: You must not have sexual relations with a woman and also with her daughter. Nor are you to marry her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter and have sexual relations with her. They are blood relatives; it is depravity.

L.17: The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover; her son's daughter and her daughter's daughter you shall not take to uncover her nakedness; they [are] relatives; it [is] depravity.

R.17: Do not have sexual relations with a woman and with her daughter too. And do not marry a woman and also her granddaughter, whether she is her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter. These women are close family. Doing this is a shameful, evil thing.

decisions.choice: a woman and her daughter ... you will not take: you must not have both, whether by marriage or otherwise
decisions.reason: To "take" a woman is to marry her (Genesis 4:19; 24:67). A man who has married a woman may not also have her daughter or granddaughter, and the ban covers any sexual relation with both. Chapter 20 punishes marrying a woman and her mother by burning (20:14).

decisions.choice: they are relatives: the women are blood relatives of one another
decisions.reason: The word is the one for "flesh" or kin in verse 6. The women are of one family, so a man may not take more than one of them.

decisions.choice: depravity: a shameful, wicked act
decisions.reason: The word names deliberate wickedness, especially in sexual matters (19:29; 20:14; Judges 20:6; Job 31:11).

decisions.choice: marry
decisions.reason: The verb is "take", which with a woman as its object means to marry her. Literal keeps "take".

decisions.choice: a shameful, evil thing
decisions.reason: Readable uses two common words for the one Hebrew word. Literal and Balanced say "depravity".

records.source: וְאִשָּׁ֥ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָ֖הּ לֹ֣א תִקָּ֑ח לִצְרֹ֗ר לְגַלּ֧וֹת עֶרְוָתָ֛הּ עָלֶ֖יהָ בְּחַיֶּֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And [a] woman to her sister not you will take, to make [her] a rival wife, to uncover her nakedness beside her in her life.
pieces: While your wife is alive, you must not also marry her sister, making the two women rivals by having sexual relations with her as well.

L.18: And a woman in addition to her sister you shall not take, to be a rival wife, to uncover her nakedness beside her in her lifetime.

R.18: Do not marry two sisters. As long as your wife is alive, do not marry her sister too and have sexual relations with her. That would make the sisters rivals.

decisions.choice: a woman to her sister: a woman's sister in addition to the woman herself
alternatives: one woman in addition to another (a ban on any second wife)
decisions.reason: In this chapter "sister" is meant literally throughout, so the verse forbids marrying two sisters at the same time. The same Hebrew phrase can also mean "one to another", as it does of curtains joined to one another (Exodus 26:3, 5, 6), and the verse has sometimes been read as a ban on taking any second wife.

decisions.choice: to make her a rival wife: to set two sisters against each other as wives of one man
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause distress or to make a rival; a related word names Peninnah, Hannah's rival wife (1 Samuel 1:6). Jacob married the sisters Leah and Rachel, and their rivalry runs through Genesis 29:30-30:24.

decisions.choice: in her lifetime: while the first wife lives
decisions.reason: The ban lasts as long as the first wife lives. Once she has died, marrying her sister is not forbidden.

decisions.choice: While your wife is alive (Balanced); As long as your wife is alive (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the time limit first and name the first woman as "your wife", which is what "a woman ... her sister" implies. Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

records.source: וְאֶל־אִשָּׁ֖ה בְּנִדַּ֣ת טֻמְאָתָ֑הּ לֹ֣א תִקְרַ֔ב לְגַלּ֖וֹת עֶרְוָתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And to [a] woman in [the] impurity of her uncleanness not you will draw near to uncover her nakedness.
pieces: While a woman is unclean because of her monthly period, you must not go near her for sexual relations.

L.19: And to a woman in the impurity of her uncleanness you shall not draw near to uncover her nakedness.

R.19: Do not have sexual relations with a woman during her monthly period, while she is unclean.

decisions.choice: the impurity of her uncleanness: the uncleanness of her monthly period
decisions.reason: The word for impurity is the one used for a woman's period in 12:2 and 15:19-24. Under 15:24 a man who lies with her then becomes unclean for seven days; here the act is forbidden outright, and 20:18 sets the penalty of being cut off. Ezekiel lists it among the sins of Israel (Ezekiel 18:6; 22:10).

decisions.choice: unclean because of her monthly period
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the cause of the uncleanness, as in 12:2. Literal keeps "the impurity of her uncleanness".

records.source: וְאֶל־אֵ֨שֶׁת֙ עֲמִֽיתְךָ֔ לֹא־תִתֵּ֥ן שְׁכָבְתְּךָ֖ לְזָ֑רַע לְטָמְאָה־בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And to [the] wife of your fellow not you will give your lying for seed, to become unclean by her.
pieces: You must not have intercourse with the wife of a fellow Israelite. It would make you unclean through her.

L.20: And to the wife of your fellow you shall not give your lying for seed, to become unclean by her.

R.20: Do not have sexual relations with another man's wife. That would make you unclean.

decisions.choice: give your lying for seed: have sexual intercourse
decisions.reason: A frank phrase for intercourse with emission of semen (compare 15:16-18; 19:20; Numbers 5:13). Here it names adultery, which the Ten Commandments forbid (Exodus 20:14) and 20:10 punishes with death for both.

decisions.choice: your fellow: a fellow member of the people
decisions.reason: The word means one's neighbor or fellow, a member of the same community (5:21; 19:11, 15, 17).

decisions.choice: to become unclean by her: the act defiles the man
decisions.reason: Sexual sin makes a person unclean, and verses 24-28 say it defiles the land as well. This uncleanness is not removed by washing, as the uncleanness of chapters 11-15 is.

decisions.choice: a fellow Israelite (Balanced); another man (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "your fellow". Balanced says who the fellow is; Readable says simply "another man's wife".

records.source: וּמִֽזַּרְעֲךָ֥ לֹא־תִתֵּ֖ן לְהַעֲבִ֣יר לַמֹּ֑לֶךְ וְלֹ֧א תְחַלֵּ֛ל אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And of your offspring not you will give to make pass over to Molech, and not you will profane [the] name of your God; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: None of your children may be handed over and made to pass through the fire to Molech. You must not profane the name of your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: And of your offspring you shall not give [any] to make [them] pass over to Molech, and you shall not profane the name of your God; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: Do not give any of your children to be burned as a sacrifice to the god Molech. That would bring shame on the name of your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Molech: a god to whom children were given in fire
decisions.reason: Molech is named as a god again in 20:2-5, where giving him a child is punished by stoning, and in 1 Kings 11:7, where he is the god of the Ammonites. The name has the same consonants as the word for "king". It has been proposed, from inscriptions found at Carthage, that the word names a kind of sacrifice rather than a god; but 20:5 speaks of people prostituting themselves "after Molech", which treats Molech as a god.

decisions.choice: give to make pass over: hand children over to be killed in fire
alternatives: dedicate children to Molech by a fire rite without killing them
decisions.reason: "Make pass over" is short for making a child "pass through the fire" (Deuteronomy 18:10; 2 Kings 16:3; 23:10). The prophets make clear that the children died: Jeremiah 7:31 and 19:5 speak of burning sons and daughters in the fire, Jeremiah 32:35 links this with Molech, and Ezekiel 16:20-21 says the children were slaughtered. Some have taken the phrase as a rite of dedication in which the child was not killed, but these passages speak of death.

decisions.choice: profane the name of your God: treat God's holy name as common and bring it into contempt
decisions.reason: Israel bears the LORD's name, so to give its children to another god dishonors him before the nations (20:3; 22:2, 32). The word for "offspring" is the word for "seed" in verse 20, which links this law with the laws around it.

decisions.choice: to make them pass over to Molech
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text is followed. The Septuagint reads differently here, with "to serve a ruler", taking the consonants of Molech as the word for "king" or "ruler". Reviewers should check the Septuagint reading.

decisions.choice: made to pass through the fire (Balanced); to be burned as a sacrifice (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "the fire" from the full form of the phrase in Deuteronomy 18:10 and 2 Kings 23:10. Readable says what was done to the children, following Jeremiah 7:31 and 32:35. Literal keeps "make [them] pass over".

decisions.choice: the god Molech
decisions.reason: Readable tells the reader that Molech is the name of a god.

records.source: וְאֶ֨ת־זָכָ֔ר לֹ֥א תִשְׁכַּ֖ב מִשְׁכְּבֵ֣י אִשָּׁ֑ה תּוֹעֵבָ֖ה הִֽוא׃
records.gloss: And with [a] male not you will lie [the] lyings of [a] woman; [an] abomination it [is].
pieces: You must not lie with a male as a man lies with a woman. It is a detestable act.

L.22: And with a male you shall not lie the lyings of a woman; it [is] an abomination.

R.22: A man must not have sexual relations with another man as he would with a woman. That is a disgusting thing.

decisions.choice: an abomination: something the LORD detests
decisions.reason: The word names what God finds abhorrent and will not accept. It is used for the gods and worship of the nations (Deuteronomy 7:25-26; 12:31), for unclean food (Deuteronomy 14:3), for dishonest weights (Deuteronomy 25:16), and for a range of wrongs in Proverbs (6:16-19). Here and in 20:13 it is stated of this act in particular, and verses 26-30 use the plural for all the practices in the chapter.

decisions.choice: lie with a male the lyings of a woman: have sexual intercourse with a male as with a woman
decisions.reason: To "lie with" is to have sexual relations. "The lyings of a woman" means the way one lies with a woman, and "the lying of a male" is used in the same way for a woman's intercourse with a man (Numbers 31:17-18, 35). The law is spoken to men, and 20:13 repeats it with the penalty of death for both men.

decisions.choice: a detestable act (Balanced); a disgusting thing (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "an abomination". Balanced and Readable use the wording for this word throughout Leviticus.

decisions.choice: A man ... with another man
decisions.reason: Readable names the man spoken to, since "you" in this chapter is the men of Israel (verse 6).

records.source: וּבְכָל־בְּהֵמָ֛ה לֹא־תִתֵּ֥ן שְׁכָבְתְּךָ֖ לְטָמְאָה־בָ֑הּ וְאִשָּׁ֗ה לֹֽא־תַעֲמֹ֞ד לִפְנֵ֧י בְהֵמָ֛ה לְרִבְעָ֖הּ תֶּ֥בֶל הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And with any animal not you will give your lying, to become unclean by it; and [a] woman not will stand before [an] animal to mate with it; confusion it [is].
pieces: You must not have intercourse with any animal; it would make you unclean. No woman is to offer herself to an animal so that it mates with her. That is a perverse mixing.

L.23: And with any animal you shall not give your lying, to become unclean by it; and a woman shall not stand before an animal to mate with it; it [is] confusion.

R.23: Do not have sexual relations with any animal. That would make you unclean. A woman must not offer herself to an animal to have sexual relations with it. That mixes what must never be mixed.

decisions.choice: a man with an animal; a woman with an animal: both are forbidden
decisions.reason: The first law is spoken to the men, the second names the woman directly. Chapter 20 punishes both with death, for the person and the animal (20:15-16; Exodus 22:19; Deuteronomy 27:21). To "stand before" an animal is to present oneself to it.

decisions.choice: confusion: a perverse mixing of what must be kept apart
decisions.reason: The word is found only here and in 20:12. It seems to come from a root meaning to mix, and it names a confusing of the order God set, as the laws against mixing kinds do (19:19).

decisions.choice: to mate with it: to copulate
decisions.reason: The verb is used of animals mating (20:16; and of breeding in 19:19).

decisions.choice: a perverse mixing (Balanced); That mixes what must never be mixed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "confusion". Balanced and Readable bring out the sense of mixing.

records.source: אַל־תִּֽטַּמְּא֖וּ בְּכָל־אֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֤י בְכָל־אֵ֨לֶּה֙ נִטְמְא֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י מְשַׁלֵּ֖חַ מִפְּנֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Do not make yourselves unclean by all these, for by all these have made themselves unclean the nations which I [am] sending away from before you.
pieces: Do not let any of these things make you unclean. All of them are what made the nations unclean, the nations I am driving out from before you.

L.24: Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these [things], for by all these the nations that I am sending away from before you have made themselves unclean.

R.24: Do not make yourselves unclean by doing any of these things. The nations that I am driving out ahead of you did all these things. That made them unclean.

decisions.choice: make yourselves unclean: be defiled by these acts
decisions.reason: Uncleanness here is not the bodily uncleanness of chapters 11-15, which washing and offerings remove. It is the defilement of wrongdoing, which stains the people who do it and, verse 25 says, the land itself (compare Numbers 35:33-34; Ezekiel 36:17).

decisions.choice: the nations I am sending away: the peoples of Canaan whom the LORD is driving out
decisions.reason: The verb means to send away or drive out (20:23; Exodus 23:28-30). The present tense says the LORD is already at work removing them.

decisions.choice: driving out
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sending away". Balanced and Readable use the usual wording for forcing a people from its land.

records.source: וַתִּטְמָ֣א הָאָ֔רֶץ וָאֶפְקֹ֥ד עֲוֺנָ֖הּ עָלֶ֑יהָ וַתָּקִ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And became unclean the land, and I visited its iniquity on it, and vomited out the land its inhabitants.
pieces: The land was made unclean, and I called it to account for its guilt; and the land vomited out the people living on it.

L.25: And the land became unclean, and I visited its iniquity upon it, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.

R.25: The land became unclean too. So I punished it for its sin, and the land vomited out the people who lived there.

decisions.choice: the land vomited out its inhabitants: the land itself threw out the people who defiled it
decisions.reason: The land is spoken of as a body that cannot keep down what poisons it. The land belongs to the LORD (25:23), and those who defile it cannot stay in it. The picture returns in verse 28 and 20:22, where Israel is warned that the same will happen to it; 26:33 speaks of Israel's scattering among the nations.

decisions.choice: I visited its iniquity upon it: I punished it for its guilt
decisions.reason: To "visit" iniquity on someone is to call them to account and punish them (Exodus 20:5; 32:34).

decisions.choice: became unclean ... vomited out: the past tense for what is still to come
decisions.reason: Israel has not yet entered Canaan (verse 3), but the verbs speak as if the land has already thrown out its people. The judgment is as good as done. Verse 28 uses the same past tense.

decisions.choice: called it to account for its guilt (Balanced); punished it for its sin (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "visited its iniquity upon it". Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means.

records.source: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֣ם אַתֶּ֗ם אֶת־חֻקֹּתַי֙ וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֔י וְלֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֔וּ מִכֹּ֥ל הַתּוֹעֵבֹ֖ת הָאֵ֑לֶּה הָֽאֶזְרָ֔ח וְהַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֥ר בְּתוֹכְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will keep, you, my statutes and my judgments, and not you will do any of all the abominations these, the native-born and the sojourner who sojourns among you,
pieces: But you are to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings and not do any of these detestable things, neither the native-born nor the outsider who lives among you,

L.26: And you, you shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments, and you shall not do any of all these abominations, the native or the sojourner who sojourns among you,

R.26: But you must keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and rules. You must not do any of these disgusting things. This is true for those born in Israel and for strangers who live among you.

decisions.choice: and you, you shall keep: you, unlike the nations
decisions.reason: The pronoun is added for emphasis and sets Israel against the nations of verses 24-25.

decisions.choice: the native-born and the sojourner: Israelite and outsider alike
decisions.reason: As in 16:29 and 17:15. These laws bind the outsider living in Israel as well, because the land itself is defiled by them.

decisions.choice: these abominations: all the practices listed in the chapter
decisions.reason: The word of verse 22 is used here in the plural for every act forbidden in verses 6-23.

decisions.choice: detestable things (Balanced); disgusting things (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 22. Literal keeps "abominations".

records.source: כִּ֚י אֶת־כָּל־הַתּוֹעֵבֹ֣ת הָאֵ֔ל עָשׂ֥וּ אַנְשֵֽׁי־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִפְנֵיכֶ֑ם וַתִּטְמָ֖א הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: for all the abominations these did [the] people of the land who [were] before you, and became unclean the land;
pieces: for the people who lived in the land before you did all these detestable things, and the land became unclean.

L.27: for all these abominations the people of the land who [were] before you did, and the land became unclean;

R.27: The people who lived in the land before you did all these disgusting things, and the land became unclean.

decisions.choice: the people of the land who were before you: the people who lived in Canaan before Israel
decisions.reason: "Before you" here means earlier in time, the people living in the land before Israel came. The same words in verse 28 have the same sense.

decisions.choice: the land became unclean: repeating verse 25
decisions.reason: The repetition presses home the warning that the next verse draws from it.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־תָקִ֤יא הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם בְּטַֽמַּאֲכֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר קָאָ֛ה אֶת־הַגּ֖וֹי אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִפְנֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: and not will vomit out the land you when you make it unclean, as it vomited out the nation which [was] before you.
pieces: Then the land will not vomit you out for making it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that was there before you.

L.28: and the land will not vomit you out when you make it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that [was] before you.

R.28: Then the land will not vomit you out for making it unclean, as it vomited out the people who lived there before you.

decisions.choice: and the land will not vomit you out: the result of keeping God's laws (verse 26)
decisions.reason: The sentence goes back to the command of verse 26: if Israel keeps the laws, the land will not throw it out. The warning is plain: Israel will not be spared what the nations suffered if it does what they did (20:22; 26:33).

decisions.choice: the nation: the peoples of Canaan taken together
decisions.reason: The singular stands for all the peoples who lived in the land, the "nations" of verse 24.

decisions.choice: Then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable begin a new sentence with "Then" to show that this is the result of obeying verse 26.

records.source: כִּ֚י כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה מִכֹּ֥ל הַתּוֹעֵב֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְנִכְרְת֛וּ הַנְּפָשׁ֥וֹת הָעֹשֹׂ֖ת מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמָּֽם׃
records.gloss: For everyone who will do any of all the abominations these, and will be cut off the persons who do [them] from [the] midst of their people.
pieces: For if anyone does any of these detestable things, the persons who do them must be cut off from the people.

L.29: For everyone who does any of all these abominations, the persons who do [them] will be cut off from among their people.

R.29: Anyone who does any of these disgusting things must be removed from the people.

decisions.choice: the persons who do them will be cut off: they will be removed from the people of God
decisions.reason: The penalty of being "cut off", as in 7:20. It applies to every act in the chapter. Chapter 20 sets out more specific penalties for many of them.

decisions.choice: the persons: any man or woman who does these things
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a living person. The penalty falls on everyone who takes part, not only on the man spoken to.

records.source: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֣ם אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֗י לְבִלְתִּ֨י עֲשׂ֜וֹת מֵחֻקּ֤וֹת הַתּֽוֹעֵבֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲשׂ֣וּ לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תִֽטַּמְּא֖וּ בָּהֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And you will keep my charge, to not do any of the customs of the abominations which have been done before you, and not you will make yourselves unclean by them; I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: Keep what I have charged you to do. Do not take up any of the detestable customs of those who lived here before you, and do not make yourselves unclean through them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"

L.30: And you shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} charge, not to do any of the customs of the abominations that have been done before you, and you shall not make yourselves unclean by them; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"

R.30: Do what I have told you. Do not follow any of the disgusting customs that the people before you followed. Do not make yourselves unclean by them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"

decisions.choice: keep my charge: carry out the duty I have laid on you
decisions.reason: The word means a charge or duty given to someone to keep, as of the priests at the tent of meeting (8:35; 22:9).

decisions.choice: the customs of the abominations ... I am the LORD your God: the chapter ends as it began
decisions.reason: "Customs" is the word of verse 3 ("their statutes"), and "I am the LORD your God" repeats verse 2. The laws of the chapter are framed by the call to be unlike the nations and by the name of the God who gives them.

decisions.choice: what I have charged you to do (Balanced); what I have told you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "my charge". Balanced and Readable say what the charge is.
